chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Shu'ayb from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Regarding the woman whose husband divorces her while she is menstruating, with one menstruation every three months, he said: If three months pass, her waiting period is complete; one menstruation is counted for each month. The resolution between these two narrations is that she only counts three months if she passes them without seeing blood at all, for she is considered pure. But if she sees blood before the completion of three months, even by one day, her waiting period is by menstruations (al-aqra'), even if that extends to fifteen months, according to what we have previously stated, and that which indicates this.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period (Iddah) for a woman with irregular menstruation who is divorced?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi uses this hadith to resolve the apparent contradiction between the general rule of counting menstruations (aqra') and the exception for irregular bleeding (istihadah) or delayed menstruation. It establishes that the three-month period serves as a definitive cutoff for iddah only when no blood is observed; otherwise, the standard rule of three menstrual cycles applies, potentially extending the waiting period up to fifteen months. This reflects the Shia juristic principle of prioritizing actual physiological signs over fixed timeframes when menstruation is irregular.
